title: QL-1.02 Mutation gate: the changed lines are broken on purpose and the tests must catch every mutant
request: Closes quality-loop principle 2 (a test that survives a mutation is a weak test). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-0.03. Quality-loop principle set of 30 October 2026 (owner's order: implement as a gate for all dev).

tasks.title: Mutation runner over the diff
requirements: scripts/gate/mutate.mjs takes --base <sha> and --test <cmd>, lists the lines added or changed between base and the working tree in files ending .mjs, .js or .cjs under src/, vendor/ and bin/, and applies one mutation at a time from a fixed operator set: === and !==, < and >=, > and <=, && and ||, true and false, + and - on numeric operands, a return value replaced by undefined, a call statement removed

before any mutant it runs the test command twice on the unmutated tree; a failure or a differing pass count there is NOISE and the run stops with exit 2, never judging a mutant (the twin's ME-MT oracle was confounded without this control)
each mutant runs in a temporary copy of the workdir that is removed in a finally block; the original tree is byte-identical after the run (checked by hashing the scope files before and after)

--json prints {status, mutants, killed, survived, invalid, timeout, ignored, noise, survivors:[{file,line,operator}], unmutated:[{file,line}]}; exit 1 when any mutant survives; a line carrying the comment mutate-ignore with a reason is skipped and counted as ignored
the script has no dependencies and its first line carries a version: comment
a NOISE run and a run with zero mutants never report survived 0 as a result: --json carries status (ok, noise, no-mutants or error) and the survived value counts only when status is ok
a mutant counts as killed only when two runs of the test command on it both fail; a mutant whose two runs disagree stops the run with exit 2 and status noise

mutants counts judged mutants only, so mutants equals killed + survived; invalid, timeout and ignored mutants have their own counts; a run that judged no mutant exits non-zero with status no-mutants and no numeric survived

the operator set also covers: a call used as a condition negated, a ! removed, a throw statement removed, a bare return; removed, ?? replaced by ||, += and -= swapped, ++ and -- swapped, an awaited call statement removed, a plain condition negated, a ternary's branches swapped, == and != swapped, ||= and &&= swapped, * and / swapped, % replaced by *, and a const initialiser replaced by undefined; --json lists under unmutated every changed line that produced no mutant

each run creates its own temporary directory with fs.mkdtempSync under os.tmpdir(), mode 0700, never a fixed path, and removes it in a finally block and on SIGINT and SIGTERM; two concurrent runs never share a copy
a --base that is empty, does not resolve to a commit, or begins with '-' stops the run with exit 2 and status error before any test runs

before judging mutants the run applies a change that keeps the meaning of every changed line (for example wrapping each changed expression in parentheses), not a comment on one line, and runs the test command once; a failure there shows the tests react to the source text, and the run stops with exit 2 and status noise

every test command runs with HOME, MEMEV_CONFIG_DIR, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, MEMEV_ROOT and MEMEV_TEST_TMP set to fresh directories inside the run's temporary directory, GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE unset, and MEMEV_NO_SERVICE, MEMEV_NO_TUNNEL and MEMEV_NO_BACKGROUND set to 1, so a mutant's tests never touch the caller's home, vault, config or repository
after the last mutant the run executes the test command once more on the unmutated tree; a failure there stops the run with exit 2 and status noise before any kill is accepted

each mutant's copy is a self-contained repository (a clone with no hard links and no alternates, or a copied .git), never a git worktree or a link to the caller's .git, so a test's git commands never change the caller's repository
the per-mutant time limit is at least five times the slower unmutated control run plus 10 s, and --json reports the limit it used
the runner is engine code, src/engine/mutation-gate.mjs, which ships in the npm package; scripts/gate/mutate.mjs is a thin wrapper that imports it and adds nothing

mutate.mjs takes --scope <glob>, repeatable, and then judges only changed lines in files that match one of the globs; its JSON output carries mutants, killed and survived for each file as well as in total

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/gate-mutate.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

the canonical criteria include ignored == 0, so a mutate-ignore line fails the contract; the mutate-ignore marker stays a feature of the command-line tool for runs outside a contract
metric criteria run through the metric verifier of SR-0.03, which keeps the command criterion's three gates; this contract adds no verifier branch to contractVerify

docs/CONTRACTS.md gives the canonical criteria with a timeout_s and states that a gate run costs up to 4 + 2N runs of the test command for N mutants (two controls, the no-op control, two runs per mutant and a closing control) and that the three canonical metrics run the gate three times per verify, each within its own timeout_s
contractSign lints the exact bytes it signs and ignores any lint result stored in the draft, because drafts are writable by any caller with write scope

contractVerify runs the canonical mutation command with the running memev's own runner in place of the workdir's scripts/gate/mutate.mjs; when the workdir's copy is not byte-identical to memev's own, the mutation metrics FAIL with a detail saying the gate is not the pinned one, except in a task whose scope names the runner itself, where memev's own copy judges the change and the difference is reported

with contracts.mutation_required on, a contract whose implement task touches src must name an explicit base sha in its spec (SR-0.03 requirement 2) and contractSign refuses one without it; the recorded base is the spec's, so signing after the change cannot move it, and an amendment that names no new base keeps the superseded contract's base; an amendment whose base differs from the superseded contract's base is BLOCKED at verify, naming the base change, until a reviewer key signs an envelope over {contract id, old base, new base}, so every base change is reviewed
contractVerify sets MEMEV_CONTRACT_BASE to the recorded base for every command, metric and red-green run, overriding any value in its own environment
